A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: early thirties — a poised, graceful face with soft contours; at most faint lines, no deep folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; warm beige skin; softly rounded face that still tapers to a small chin; rounder almond eyes of natural size; coral-orange eyes; gently arched, slender brows; a straight nose with a slim bridge; slender lips of natural width.
Body and hair: willowy and long-limbed with soft curves — a full bust, rounded hips and a slender waist build; a shoulder-length layered bob with wispy parted bangs; pale liquid-silver hair with a bright sun-gold crown, circled by thin rings of light like orbits.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: a quiet, thoughtful look, lips lightly closed.
Her element, carried in her design: copernicium: a synthetic superheavy element first made in 1996, a single atom caught by firing zinc ions at a lead target, and named on the birthday of the astronomer who put the sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the heavens, a quiet revolution he held back for decades and printed only in the year he died; its first proposed symbol had to be changed because it had once belonged to another element; it sits below zinc, cadmium and mercury, its outer electrons held so tightly that it was predicted to flow like mercury or drift like a noble gas, and a few atoms showed it to be a volatile metal that clings only lightly to gold.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a fitted bodice and a long bustled ball gown sweeping out behind her, long gloves — an elegant, wide-trailing shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Design idea: thin overlapping liquid-silver segments separated by narrow open spaces, expressing fleeting volatile metal atoms.
Colours: liquid mercury silver, sun-centre gold, deep celestial blue, pale orbit-line white.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1900, a vast clockwork orrery hall in a cathedral town by a lagoon: brass planets on long arms slowly circling a golden gas-flame sun at the centre of a round hall, a great steam winding room turning its gears, and an observation balcony where the officers of the orrery corps reset the planets each day.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Cn) and atomic number (112) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
